title: Main menu UI: Play / Controls / Credits + sub-screens + boot wiring
description:
User request: a simple menu of Play, Controls, Credits, drawn over the attract backdrop (island1-7u5i). Flow: island1-tpz8 state machine owns nav and transitions; this issue is the UI + wiring.

## Design

PS1 8x8 font look: uppercase text via r_text_2d, selection highlight via r_rect_2d band (mirror the draw_compass bg pattern, game.c:1245).

Layout:
- Title text at the top ("ISLAND", moderate scale ~3), items stacked below (centered or lower-left - pick what reads over the backdrop at 16:9 and 4:3).
- Selected item: full-alpha white text + rect band behind + a small ">" marker; unselected items dimmed (alpha ~0.6). Item spacing ~2x glyph height.
- Nav: ACT_MENU_UP/DOWN cycles with wrap; ACT_MENU_CONFIRM activates; ACT_MENU_BACK returns from sub-screens. Guard with input_pressed edges (holding must not scroll).

Transitions:
- Confirm on PLAY -> MENU_SCREEN_PLAY: gameplay HUD back on, chase cam restored, sim resumes.
- Confirm on CONTROLS/CREDITS -> sub-screen; BACK returns to MAIN (selection preserved).
- Confirm on CREDITS -> credits text; static list is fine for v1 (dialog.c has a typewriter - reuse only if trivial). BACK returns.

CONTROLS screen content (mirror main.c's header comment; per-platform wording later for PSP/DC):
    W/S  THROTTLE/BRAKE   A/D OR ARROWS  STEER
    SHIFT BOOST           E  INTERACT    F  ENTER/EXIT CAR
    RMB DRAG LOOK         C  DEV FLY CAM F3 DEBUG STATS
    ESC  QUIT             R  DEV RESET

Boot wiring (desktop main.c):
- Core gates internally (island1-tpz8), so main.c should need no loop changes - verify boot to INTRO -> MAIN, and that Play resumes the paused sim without a catch-up burst (main.c drops backlog at MAX_TICKS anyway, but reset the accumulator on the PLAY transition if a burst is visible).

Sound: no audio in the engine yet - menu sounds are future work, not here.

title: Render pass system with fixed-function state management
description:
Render passes as FrameScene emitters: core emits ordered draw items (sky/ocean/terrain/props/vehicle/particles/beacon/HUD) into the frame; the backend (RenderAPI, see render-abstraction issue) flushes them in order. State (fog, blend, 2D mode) is a flag on the item, not ad-hoc glEnable/glDisable.

Passes live in core as emitters:

    emit_sky(&frame), emit_ocean(&frame, t), emit_terrain(&frame),
    emit_props(&frame), emit_buildings(&frame), emit_vehicle(&frame, car),
    emit_particles(&frame), emit_beacon(&frame), emit_hud(&frame)

Each appends items with flags (fog on/off, alpha, 2D). The desktop backend diffs its own GL state between items — that's where today's gfx.c state manager goes (backend/desktop, NOT core). 2D/alpha items are self-contained (begin+end their own state), replacing push/pop semantics.

- Fog color == sky color so the horizon seam is invisible (island1-a440).

comments.text:
## Audit context (2026-10-03, docs/render.md)

Gribb-Hartmann plane extraction + conservative AABB test exist but are locked in src/core/game.c:272-324 (frustum_plane, extract_frustum, aabb_in_frustum) and used only by ocean cells (game.c:371). Car, parcel, wake and billboards are recorded unconditionally; island content (terrain island1-39q6, props, characters island1-urkr) would not be culled at all.

## Why it matters per platform

- Desktop: fine today (tiny scene, F3 shows usage), needed before island content pushes against R_MAX_DRAWS/R_MAX_VERTS (island1-41ct).
- PSP/DC: vertex throughput is THE bottleneck. HW clipping exists (GE clips polys; PVR TA clips) but the hardware still vertex-processes every submitted poly — culling before recording is the only culling that saves transform + submission work.

## Design details

- Keep the conservative AABB test (reject only when fully outside one plane) — matches the fog-heavy PS1 look, no pop-in at plane edges.
- Mesh gains world-space bounds: float center[3]; float radius; grown incrementally in mesh_make/mesh_add_quad. Cull with the transform applied: transform the center, scale the radius by the max scale factor of the world matrix (current meshes don't scale, but billboards/props might later).
- Sphere test (center+radius vs plane) is cheaper per draw than AABB; AABB stays for ocean cells.
- Extend the F3 overlay with a CULLED counter next to the OCEAN drawn/total cells counter.

Done when: frustum code lives in core with no duplicates, meshes carry bounds, car/parcel/props cull correctly (F3 counters), ocean behaviour unchanged.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Verification correction (2026-10-03)

The original note "the console targets cannot express the other modes" was wrong for the Dreamcast. Verified against KOS:

- DC: fog is per-polygon-header (PVR_FOG_TABLE / PVR_FOG_VERTEX / PVR_FOG_TABLE2 / PVR_FOG_DISABLE, dc/pvr/pvr_header.h) and KOS exports pvr_fog_table_linear / _exp / _exp2 / _custom, pvr_fog_table_color, pvr_fog_far_depth and the PVR_FOG_DENSITY register. DC can do linear (table), exp and exp2 — and table fog is perspectively correct (built from an inverse-w depth table, pvr_fog_tables.h).
- PSP: GE fog is linear only — sceGuFog(near, far, color) has no mode/density parameter (verified: pspsdk src/gu/sceGuFog.c); GU_FOG is just an enable bit.
- Desktop: GL_LINEAR hardcoded at init (gfx_gl.c:36); GL 1.5 also has EXP/EXP2/density. The comment there (EXP default swallows everything) is good context for why the mode must match what the passes configure.

## Revised recommendation

Keep linear as the frame's only mode — it matches the PSP exactly and the art direction (docs/art-direction.md: linear fog, colour = sky_horizon). The DC could honour a hypothetical EXP mode (pvr_fog_table_exp) but we would never use it. Document linear-only (done in docs/render.md) rather than adding mode+density.

title: RenderAPI: per-draw alpha test for cutout textures
description:
Context: GL 1.5 audit (2026-10-03, docs/render.md) found only a `blend` flag in RDraw/GfxState. Cutout textures (tree canopies, fences, stippled spray per docs/art-direction.md) need per-pixel discard: cheaper than blending on every target and needs no transparent sorting.

Change:
- RDraw gains `int alpha_test;` + `float alpha_ref;` (default 0 = off; 0.5 typical). Mutually exclusive with `blend` per draw.
- Desktop (base island1-1dtz): GfxState gains the fields; gfx_set() does glEnable(GL_ALPHA_TEST)/glAlphaFunc(GL_GREATER, ref); render_gl draw_state_from() maps them.
- PSP backend (island1-gi02): native - sceGuEnable(GU_ALPHA_TEST) + sceGuAlphaFunc(GU_GREATER, ref, 0xff) (pspsdk pspgu.h: GU_ALPHA_TEST = 0).
- Dreamcast backend (island1-fo7c): native equivalent is the punch-through polygon list (PVR_LIST_PT_POLY) - submit alpha-tested draws there (KOS kernel/arch/dreamcast/include/dc/pvr/pvr_header.h).

Done when: a masked texture (e.g. tree canopy with holes) renders cut out on desktop with no sorting artefacts; the flag survives the backend split.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Audit context (2026-10-03, docs/render.md)

The GL 1.5 fixed-function audit found no path to glAlphaTest: RDraw/GfxState carry only a `blend` flag, and draw_state_from() (src/backend/desktop/render_gl.c:77) pins every draw to blend/depth/cull. Meanwhile cutout textures are core to the art direction (docs/art-direction.md): tree canopies with holes, fences, stippled spray edges (island1-5stj). Alpha test is the right primitive for all of these — cheaper than blending on every target (no blend fill-rate, no transparent sorting) and it composes with the PS1 look (hard-edged cutouts).

## Hardware mapping (verified against SDK sources)

- PSP: GU_ALPHA_TEST = 0 state + sceGuAlphaFunc(int func, int value, int mask), GU_NEVER..GU_GEQUAL (pspsdk src/gu/sceGuAlphaFunc.c; the sprite sample uses sceGuAlphaFunc(GU_GREATER, 0, 0xff)). Reference is 0..255 with an AND mask — the backend converts from our 0..1 float.
- Dreamcast: punch-through polygon list PVR_LIST_PT_POLY (KOS dc/pvr/pvr_header.h) — native per-pixel alpha discard, no blending, and it sorts with the opaque pass, so no transparent-sorting artefacts.
- Desktop: glEnable(GL_ALPHA_TEST) + glAlphaFunc(GL_GREATER, ref) — add fields to GfxState and the diff in gfx_set().

## Design notes

- RDraw gains `int alpha_test;` + `float alpha_ref;` (default 0 = off, 0.5 typical). Keep alpha_test and blend mutually exclusive per draw — on DC they are literally different lists, so a draw cannot be both; assert it on desktop and document it.
- On DC the backend picks PT_POLY when alpha_test is set, TR_POLY when blend is set, OP_POLY otherwise — the list choice falls out of the flags.
- Related: island1-01nc (tex_env ADD for glow is a separate concern); island1-fo7c / island1-gi02 consume this flag.

Done when: a masked canopy texture renders cut out on desktop with no sorting artefacts when overlapping; the flag survives the backend split (test on PPSSPP/redream emulators).

title: Dreamcast audio backend: miniaudio native KOS backend, single-threaded mixer pumped from game loop
description:
Implement the Dreamcast side of the audio contract (island1-850o) using miniaudio dev-0.12s built-in native KallistiOS backend (ma_backend_dreamcast, talks straight to AICA via snd_init/snd_mem_malloc -- no GLdc-style external glue needed, this is the whole reason to move to dev-0.12 rather than staying on an older miniaudio).

Pattern to follow almost verbatim: /Users/haydenkowalchuk/Documents/dc/integrity/src/dreamcast/sys_sound.c -- ma_context_init(NULL, 0, ...) auto-selects the dreamcast backend when compiled for KOS; ma_device_config with MA_THREADING_MODE_SINGLE_THREADED, ma_format_s16, 2 channels, 44100Hz, periodSizeInFrames 2048, noFixedSizedCallback MA_TRUE; a custom dataCallback that mixes one active ma_decoder voice (their v1) into the output buffer, padding with silence when the decoder runs dry; explicit ma_device_step(device, MA_BLOCKING_MODE_NON_BLOCKING) called from the main loop (SND_Update equivalent) rather than relying on a background thread -- KOS threading is cooperative enough that driving the mixer from the game tick is more predictable and avoids cross-thread state races without extra locking.

This is NOT ma_engine territory on DC -- their example deliberately stays on the low-level ma_context/ma_device API, likely because ma_engine pulls in a resource-manager job system with its own threads that is heavier than16MB main RAM + AICA VRAM budget wants, and the single-threaded pump gives deterministic mixing tied to the frame tick. Expand their single-voice dataCallback into a small software voice pool (music stream + a few concurrent SFX voices, e.g. 4-8, mixed additively in the callback) once the basic path works -- AICA has limited hardware voices so all mixing happens in SH4 software before one stereo buffer is pushed to the sound RAM window.

Constraint check: AICA sound RAM (VRAM) is small (~2MB total across all voices), so period buffers uploaded via snd_mem_malloc must stay modest (the 2048-frame period in the reference is already sized for this). Music must stream (ma_decoder pulls a chunk at a time, never the whole file resident); SFX can be fully resident PCM since they are short.

Wire into src/backend/dreamcast/audio_dc.c, compiled alongside render_dc.c in the dreamcast branch of src/meson.build, linking miniaudio_dep and -lpthread (already flagged in the subprojects miniaudio meson.build). Init/shutdown/pump hooked from main_dc.c next to the existing pvr_init/frame loop.

Done when: DC build (build_dc, island.cdi) boots in an emulator or on hardware, plays a looping music track and fires a one-shot SFX on the delivery toast without audio glitches or crashes across repeated scene transitions; no thread-related asserts or deadlocks from KOS.

   - snd_stream_alloc(callback, SND_STREAM_BUFFER_MAX=64KiB), memalign(32) drv_buf.
   - snd_stream_start_adpcm(shnd, 44100, channels-1) - headerless interleaved AICA ADPCM, stereo, 44.1kHz, 1 byte = 1 stereo frame; duration = bytes/44100.

title: Dialog textbox: text cut off on PSP/Dreamcast, no scroll/overflow
description:
Report: on small screens (PSP 480x272, Dreamcast 640x480) conversation text does not flow cleanly in the box - it is cut off and never scrolls, so the player cannot read the whole message.

Investigate src/core/dialog.c: dialog_box() geometry vs viewport, wrap function (row count vs box height), font scale, speaker row, DIALOG_MAX_LINES 4 / DIALOG_MAX_CHARS 96 capacity, and what happens when wrapped rows exceed visible rows (currently nothing - hard cut).

Fix direction: wrap against the real inner box width at every target resolution; guarantee the box fits speaker + N wrapped rows; when a line wraps past the visible rows, scroll (follow the typewriter reveal so the last revealed row stays visible) or paginate on E. Verify at 480x272 and 640x480 as well as desktop 1280x720.

Done when: a max-length line (96 chars) is fully readable at 480x272 (all rows reachable via scroll/pagination), no row is clipped mid-glyph, desktop behavior unchanged, dialog test + full suite green, PSP build green.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
Root cause confirmed (src/core/dialog.c):

Box = 70% w x 1/3 h of viewport. At PSP 480x272: box 336x90, fixed text scale 2 (16px cells), inner_w 320 -> 20 chars/row; after the speaker-name row only 52px remain -> max_rows = 52/18 = 2. wrap_line() silently caps at max_rows, so 40 of ~86 chars are shown and the rest is thrown away forever - no scroll, no paging. (Dreamcast 640x480 gets 27 chars/row x 6 rows = fine for current <=96-char lines, but still truncates silently if a line ever wraps past DIALOG_MAX_LINES=4.) The 8x8 font has no arrow glyph (0x1F blank) for a "more" indicator.

Fix in dialog.c / dialog.h:
1. Shared dialog_layout(): picks text scale from {2.0, 1.0} (integer scales only - fractional scale misaligns the run-merged glyph quads) such that the longest line of the conversation wraps into rows that fit the box at that scale (fit includes the speaker row). PSP falls to scale 1: 40 chars/row, 3 rows for an 86-char line vs 6 that fit => one page, nothing lost. Desktop/DC stay at scale 2 (unchanged).
2. Hard guarantee: wrap ALL rows (cap DIALOG_WRAP_ROWS 16, separate from DIALOG_MAX_LINES which is conversation line count) and page them with E. E rule: incomplete -> complete; complete + rows below -> next page (s_page += fit_rows); complete + last page -> next line/close. page resets on line change/start. Getters dialog_page()/dialog_page_count() for tests/game.
3. Blinking down-triangle (4 stacked rects, no font glyph needed) bottom-right whenever more pages exist; existing blinking "E" hint unchanged when line complete.
4. hud_dialog_draw() gains a page parameter (callers: dialog_draw + dialog_test only).

Tests: existing 6 sections must stay green (320x180 viewport, short lines -> scale 2, 1 page, E rule unchanged); new sections: 86-char line at r_viewport(480,272) -> dialog_page_count()==1 (PSP fix); 96-char line at r_viewport(240,160) -> page_count()>1, exactly page_count() E presses to page through and close.

title: App flow: screen state machine (intro/menu/play) + menu-nav input actions
description:
Foundation for the front-end (user request: intro screens + main menu). Context: main.c boots straight into gameplay; there is no top-level flow. GameMode (GAME_MODE_DRIVE/FOOT, game.h:25) is player stance and must not be overloaded for app flow.

## Design

New src/core/menu.{h,c} owning the front-end:

    typedef enum {
        MENU_SCREEN_INTRO,    /* title splash sequence */
        MENU_SCREEN_MAIN,     /* main menu over the attract backdrop */
        MENU_SCREEN_CONTROLS, /* sub-screen */
        MENU_SCREEN_CREDITS,  /* sub-screen */
        MENU_SCREEN_PLAY      /* live gameplay */
    } MenuScreen;
    void menu_init(void);        /* starts on INTRO */
    MenuScreen menu_screen(void);
    void menu_tick(float dt);    /* input edges + timed intro fades + sub-screen nav */
    void menu_render(void);      /* records OVERLAY UI onto the already-recorded frame */

- game.c gates on menu_screen(): when != PLAY, skip drive/quest/npc/walk ticks, suppress the gameplay HUD, and use the menu attract camera (separate issue). game_tick()/game_render() stay the only backend entry points, so desktop main.c needs no loop changes - core gates internally. menu_tick runs before the gameplay gates inside game_tick(); menu_render records after the scene emitters inside game_render() (r_frame_begin() lives there, so appended OVERLAY draws reach the backend in the same frame).
- Input contract: add menu-nav actions to input.h in the gameplay-contract section (before ACT_DEV_*):
  ACT_MENU_UP, ACT_MENU_DOWN, ACT_MENU_CONFIRM, ACT_MENU_BACK
  Desktop bindings in input_glfw.c: Up/W, Down/S, Enter/Space (confirm), Esc/Backspace (back). ACT_PAUSE/ACT_QUIT keep their current behaviour (ESC still quits during PLAY; no pause menu in v1).
- Tests include menu.h directly (game.c includes it too). Keep the screen enum in menu.h, not game.h - game.h only forwards what debug tooling needs.
- Style: snake_case, s_ statics, single precision (menu timing in seconds with dt clamped like the chase spring).

## Done when
meson compile -C build warning-free; new GL-free test (tests/menu_test.c + meson test target in src/meson.build) asserts INTRO -> (skip) -> MAIN -> (confirm) -> PLAY, PLAY is stable (no back-exit in v1), and the four new actions produce pressed edges; desktop boots to the intro.

title: PSP near-clip rewrite in render_gu.c

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text: Test of comment writing.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## What was broken in the WIP near clip (src/backend/psp/render_gu.c)

1. mat4_mul_vec4 read flat[0..3] (column 0 of a GL column-major matrix) as if it were row 0, so it multiplied by the transpose.
2. mat4_mul4 computed B*A^T instead of A*B (with B = I it returned A^T), so the value called "mvp" was actually proj*view^T.
3. The near-plane test was `z >= 0`. A GL perspective projection puts the eye plane at z + w = 0, so that test throws away the whole near half of the frustum (z/w in [-1,0)) - most of the scene disappears.
4. Emitted vertices were perspective-divided to NDC but submitted with GU_TRANSFORM_3D while apply_state installed the real proj/view, so the GE projected them a second time.
5. clip_vert_lerp assigned out->v twice and never interpolated colour.
6. The quad path could overrun its count*2 vertex reservation: a clipped triangle fans out to 6 vertices, so quads need 3*count.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
## Fix

Keep the GE's real proj/view: hardware fog is derived from view space (PPSSPP emits `v_fogdepth = viewPos.z * coef`), so swapping in identity matrices for CPU-transformed draws would kill fog on the ocean and other recorded draws. Instead: transform each triangle to clip space, clip against `z + w >= 0`, then map the clipped vertices back through `(proj*view)^-1` to object space before writing them. `M^-1 (M obj) = obj` with w == 1, so the GE's forward transform lands exactly on the clipped clip-space vertex. Fully-inside triangles are emitted unchanged (no inverse), and screen-space draws skip the transform entirely (orthographic, w = 1, never crosses the plane).

`emit_tri` / `emit_v` / `clip_vert_from` absorb the quad-vs-triangle duplication, so `present_recorded` is 64 lines instead of 111, and the GE-state reset repeated in `render_init`/`render_present` is now `reset_ge_state()`.

Verified with a standalone harness in /tmp/clip_test.c covering: mat4_mul_vec4 vs. a hand-written GL column-major multiply, `mvp*inv == I`, near-plane sign for in-frustum / just-past-znear / between-eye-and-near / behind-eye points, object->clip->inverse->object round trip, 1-in/2-out -> 3 verts, 2-in/1-out -> 4 verts, fully-behind dropped, and NDC reproduction after the inverse+forward hop. PSP target builds clean (`meson compile -C build_psp`), desktop suite 8/8.

title: PSP renderer needs near-plane clipping for world-space draws
description:
The PSP GE's clipper behaves differently from the Dreamcast TA. Our DC backend does manual near-plane clipping for world-space triangles (dc_clip_near) before submitting; the PSP backend submits transformed vertices directly via sceGuDrawArray for meshes and builds GuVtx from recorded verts without explicit software near clipping. Vertices that go behind the near plane (w <= 0) can produce incorrect or disappearing geometry on hardware/PPSSPP in some cases.

## Acceptance
- Investigate PSP recorded path (render_gu.c present_recorded) and mesh path: do we need to clip against near plane before building display list vertices?
- Add conservative clipping where needed or document why not required.
- Test on PPSSPP and real hardware if available.
- Keep core platform-agnostic (clipping logic lives in backend/psp).

Mentioned while debugging DC trail depth/visibility (island1-m4g4 follow-up).

title: Player mode state machine: on-foot/in-vehicle, entering and exiting
description:
Toggle between on-foot and in-vehicle. Car stays parked where you exit. Carried package transfers between modes.

## Design
src/player.c/h:

    typedef enum { MODE_ON_FOOT, MODE_IN_VEHICLE } PlayerMode;

    typedef struct {
        PlayerMode mode;
        vec3  pos; float heading;   // on-foot state
        float transition_t;         // 0.5 s crossfade
    } Player;
    // vehicle state lives in CarState (island1-9n0n)

Entering:
    near a car (dist < 3.0 m) AND |car.speed| < 1.0 m/s AND press ACT_BOARD
    -> hide humanoid, mode = IN_VEHICLE, camera blends to vehicle framing

Exiting:
    in vehicle AND |car.speed| < 1.0 m/s AND press ACT_EXIT
    -> place player beside car (car right vector * 1.2 m), mode = ON_FOOT,
       car stays put (vel = 0, no idle drift)

- Add ACT_BOARD/ACT_EXIT to input actions (island1-ibqg); both bound to F as one context key
- Carried package moves with the player; delivery target is not reset on mode switch (island1-draq)
- On-foot camera: reuse chase cam (island1-fnss) with distance 4.5 / height 1.9 (vs 7.0/3.2 in vehicle); lerp params during transition_t

## Done when
Enter/exit works anywhere (land or water) when stopped; no flicker between body and car during transition; on-foot camera framing matches PS1 references; carried package and target persist across the switch.

title: Audio asset pipeline: format policy, directory layout, per-platform path resolution, meson copy rules
description:
Decide and wire the audio asset side, independent of any single backend (can proceed in parallel with the backend pellets once island1-850o defines the ID/path registry).

Format policy (decided, user-confirmed): WAV + MP3 only, no OGG/Vorbis consideration.
  - SFX: WAV (uncompressed PCM). Short one-shots, zero decode risk, works identically across all three backends on day one, no patent/licensing surface to reason about. Keep them mono and modestly downsampled (e.g. 22050Hz) to stay small -- PS1-style aesthetic does not need more.
  - Music: MP3. miniaudio dev-0.12 has a built-in MP3 decoder (MA_HAS_MP3, no external library needed, same tier as the built-in WAV and FLAC decoders), roughly10:1 compression, streams well from UMD/CD.

Directory layout, matching the existing textures convention (assets/textures/*.png):
  assets/audio/sfx/*.wav
  assets/audio/music/*.mp3

Per-platform path resolution: reuse the exact same search pattern already proven for textures -- src/backend/psp/texture_gu.c and main.c already walk disc0:/PSP_GAME/USRDIR/assets, host0:/assets, ms0:/PSP/GAME/island/assets; src/backend/dreamcast/texture_dc.c already resolves /cd/assets. Factor that into a shared helper (or mirror it) so audio_init does not have to reinvent per-platform path probing -- this is the same class of problem, just a different file extension.

Meson wiring: extend the existing custom_target copy rules in src/meson.build (the psp-copy-assets / dreamcast equivalents already sync the whole assets/ tree, so audio may come along for free -- verify, do not assume) and confirm the final EBOOT.PBP / island.cdi / island.iso sizes stay sane once a couple of real music tracks land (a few MB each is fine on both UMD and CD-R; watch total ISO growth).

Asset registry: the ID-to-path table lives in core (audio.h consumers index by enum/int), so adding a new sound is a one-line enum entry + one file dropped in assets/audio/, no backend code changes.

Done when: a real .wav SFX and a real .mp3 music file are committed under assets/audio/ (even placeholder/scratch tones are fine for now, real musical content can come later), load correctly through the path resolver on all three platforms, and the ISO/PBP/CDI packaging still succeeds.

comments.author: mcp-agent
comments.text:
REVISION (user-approved): format policy changed, and assets are NOT committed to this repo.

SOURCE FORMAT - WAV masters are the single source of truth (MP3 policy from the description above is dropped):
- Music: 44.1kHz stereo WAV masters. DC converts to headerless interleaved AICA ADPCM via KOS wav2adpcm -n -i -t (confirmed present at /opt/toolchains/dc/kos/utils/wav2adpcm). Desktop streams the WAV via miniaudio (MA_SOUND_FLAG_STREAM). 1 byte = 1 stereo frame on DC; duration = filesize/44100.
- SFX: mono WAV masters (suggest 22050Hz to match wipeout-dc's proven AICA usage). DC converts to headerless raw PCM (8-bit signed recommended, matching wipeout's snd_sfx_load_raw_buf usage; write a small host tool in tools/ - Python is fine, no runtime decoder needed on DC). Desktop loads the WAV directly.

ASSET LOCATION - submodule, not committed here (user-confirmed): audio assets live in a git submodule (or similar external checkout) that is present locally at build time; meson points at that directory. Follow the same pattern the repo already uses for any external/vendored content. Do NOT assume assets/audio/ inside this repo - verify the actual path resolution when the submodule lands. Texture-style per-platform probing still applies (ASSET_DIR env on desktop, /cd/assets on DC, disc0:/PSP_GAME/USRDIR/assets etc on PSP) but pointed at the submodule-backed tree.

BUILD-TIME CONVERSION (DC): add meson custom_target(s) invoking wav2adpcm for each music track and the host SFX conversion tool for each SFX, emitting .adpcm / raw PCM next to the build so the DC CDI packaging picks them up (existing custom_target copy rules already sync the assets tree - verify, don't assume, per the original note). Keep conversion outputs out of git.

Registry: ID-to-path table stays in core (audio.h consumers index by enum/int); adding a sound = one enum entry + one WAV in the submodule, no backend code changes. Desktop path = raw WAV; DC path = converted artifact (registry maps per-platform via the backend's chosen extension/root).
